item.title: Saudi civil defence issues all clear for Riyadh minutes after danger alert
item.description:
Saudi civil defence issues all clear for Riyadh minutes after danger alert

Saudi Civil Defence authorities issue all clear for Riyadh City, minutes after warning residents of a “potential danger” and urging them to proceed to the nearest safe place in the capital.

Earlier, similar all clear messages were issued by the General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defense for the city of Dammam and the provinces of al-Ahsa and Abqaiq, minutes are warning residents of potential danger.

item.title: Iran executes three men convicted over January 2026 protests
item.description:
Iran executes three men convicted over January 2026 protests

Iran on Sunday executed three men convicted of taking part in armed unrest during protests in January 2026 and carrying out operations for Israel and the United States, state media reported.

On Saturday, citing judiciary's Mizan Online website, AFP reported the execution of an Iranian,  Mohammad Aref Shahbakhsh, an "operative linked to the terrorist group Jaish al-Zolm (al-Adl)".

Jaish al-Adl is an outlawed militant group in Sistan-Baluchistan province, which has long seen clashes between security forces and armed groups, including Sunni militants and members of the ethnic Baloch minority.

Iran accuses arch-enemies the United States and Israel of supporting armed groups there.

item.title: Iran tells Russia talks with US without guarantees won't end conflict, report says
item.description:
Iran tells Russia talks with US without guarantees won't end conflict, report says

Iran’s ambassador to Moscow Kazem Jalali has said Iran and Russia have discussed strengthening military and security cooperation, with Tehran stressing that talks with the US could not end the conflict without credible guarantees, according to Mehr News Agency.

Jalali said that during a three-hour meeting, Major General Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, briefed Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tehran’s strategic priorities, including accelerating construction of the Rasht-Astara railway and completing the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).

Jalali said Rezaei conveyed Tehran’s position that negotiations with Washington could not end the conflict without credible guarantees, citing repeated "US violations of commitments" during previous diplomatic engagements, Mehr reported.

He said Rezaei also explained Iran’s response to a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, stressing that dialogue alone could not provide a basis for ending the war.

According to Jalali, Rezaei cited several instances in which Iran had come under attack during diplomatic initiatives, including negotiations in Oman and Geneva, as well as engagements surrounding the Islamabad MoU.

The ambassador said Tehran had made acceptance of its seven strategic conditions by Washington a prerequisite for any new diplomatic initiative. He added that Moscow understood Iran’s position and agreed that commitments had to be implemented.

item.title: Saudi and Qatari foreign ministers discuss de-escalation efforts
item.description:
Saudi and Qatari foreign ministers discuss de-escalation efforts

Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan discussed “ongoing efforts to de-escalate tensions, and enhance security and stability” with Qatari Prime Minister and and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry said.

The discussion over a phone call came a day after Al Thani said mediation efforts between the United States and Iran were ongoing to prevent an escalation.

“We cannot wait to reach a perfect agreement; we hope to reach a good agreement,” he said.

It was the second reported phone call between the two ministers in the past week.

item.description:

  • Listen to the podcast: Chris Bowen on how he’ll reach consensus at Cop31

Australia has been urged to set aside support for its near US$100bn fossil fuel export industries and fight for a global agreement to move away from coal, gas and oil as its climate change minister, Chris Bowen, leads negotiations between nearly 200 countries at UN talks this week.

Delegates will gather in the Turkish Mediterranean resort city of Antalya on Monday for Cop31, two weeks of climate talks held amid geopolitical turmoil, with conflict in the Middle East driving an oil price crisis that has raised living costs across the globe.

item.description:
Trump still considering new assault on Iran nuclear sites – though threats less credible after Vance remarks

Qatar, the lead mediator in the US-Iran conflict, is seeking to persuade Tehran to allow UN nuclear weapons inspectors to visit Iran’s bombed nuclear sites, including those housing the country’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium.

Iran would not be required to make any commitment that the stockpile would be removed from the country, with other options on the table, including reducing the uranium content by down-blending it.

item.title: What Marco Rubio’s sidestepping of New Delhi says about the US’s stance on India
item.description:
Rubio’s decision not to meet Narendra Modi last week was seen by some as a snub – but by focusing on business leaders and oil, the secretary of state made American priorities clear. Plus: the artist bringing a female perspective to men’s clothing

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

When the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, visited India for the second time this year, headlines concentrated on who he met and where he went.

The fact that Rubio bypassed New Delhi and did not meet the prime minister, Narendra Modi, during his trip last week, and instead traveled to the financial capital, Mumbai, where he met India’s foreign minister, Subrahmanyam Jaishankar (pictured top with Rubio), and business leaders, did not go unnoticed. Nor did his decision to travel to Jamnagar, the small Gujarati town that is home to Reliance Industries’ colossal oil refinery complex.
